I diagnosed the problem class by building an end-to-end reproduction and verifying both the failure and the fix. Solution written to `/workspace/solution.md`.

## Summary

**Two stacked causes:**

1. **Hook hijack** — global `~/.gitconfig` set `core.hooksPath=/var/tmp/foreign-hooks`, which *replaces* the repo's `.git/hooks`. The repo-owned boardctl-wrapped gitreins hook (DEGRADED → exit 0) never ran. Instead a pinned guard-only hook (`gitreins guard --quality-async; exit $?`) ran and exited **2** whenever guard reported DEGRADED (`allow_skips` unset). Git normalizes a failing `pre-commit` to abort with **rc 1**, printing nothing but the hook's own banner.

2. **Pipeline masking** — `git commit ... 2>&1 | tail -3; echo rc=$?` reports `tail`'s exit status (always 0), discarding git's real rc. Result: abort invisible, HEAD unchanged, "rc=0".

**Fix:**
```bash
git config --local core.hooksPath .git/hooks
```
Local config overrides the global setting, restoring the repo-owned hook. Also stop piping `git commit` when rc matters (use bare `$?`, `$(…); rc=$?`, `${PIPESTATUS[0]}`, or `set -o pipefail`).

**Verified in an isolated repro:**
- Before: pipe idiom → `rc=0`, HEAD moves? **NO**; subprocess → `returncode=1` with only the DEGRADED banner.
- `git config --show-origin --get-all core.hooksPath` → global `/var/tmp/foreign-hooks` shadowing local `.git/hooks`.
- After: repo hook runs (advisory, exit 0), commit succeeds, HEAD advances, rc=0 truthfully reported.
- Regression check: forced failure yields `rc=0` via the tail idiom but `rc=1` via `PIPESTATUS[0]`/capture.

Reproduction artifacts were cleaned up afterward.

signatures.description: Foreman commits in a gitreins-guarded Python repo repeatedly exited 0 via the idiom `git commit ... 2>&1 | tail -3; echo rc=$?` while HEAD never moved. Two stacked causes. (1) The global ~/.gitconfig set core.hooksPath=/var/tmp/foreign-hooks, replacing the repo real hook (boardctl-wrapped gitreins hook whose DEGRADED arm exits 0) with a pinned guard-only hook `gitreins guard --quality-async; exit $?` that exits 2 whenever guard reports DEGRADED (skipped lanes) - and allow_skips deliberately unset. git commit aborts with rc 1 and prints NOTHING beyond the hook output, so there is no error line to notice; HEAD stays. (2) The shell idiom `git commit ... | tail -3; echo rc=$?` reports the PIPE (tail) exit code 0, hiding the abort. Diagnosis path that worked: run the commit under python subprocess capturing rc directly (revealed rc=1 with only the DEGRADED banner on stderr), then diff the two hook scripts and check `git config --show-origin --get-all core.hooksPath`. Fix: git config --local core.hooksPath .git/hooks to re-point at the repo-owned hooks (gitreins refuse-install error names this exact remedy), plus never pipe git commit through tail when the rc matters.
